messages:
Noah: Morning — saw intermittent GPU p99 spikes on eu-west dedicated racks around 04:10 UTC. GPUs idle-ish but NIC tx queues filling, then drops. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/eu-west/packet-spray
Ivy: Looks like "packet spray" from many tiny inference RPCs. Not CPU, not memory. NIC hw queue + driver drops correlate with stalls.
Harper: If we keep applying pool-wide caps we throttle everyone. Suggest a targeted mitigation: detect short-packet spray per-tenant and deflect small requests to a short backoff path (retryable 429) at proxy level, plus label node for scheduler avoidance.
Noah: PoC config (proxy):
```
packet_spray_deflector:
  enabled: true
  short_packet_ms: 150
  detect_rps: 1000
  action: soft_deflect_with_retry_header
  tenant_overrides:
    T-alpha: {detect_rps: 800}
```
Ivy: Important: include structured Retry-After and header so SDKs can backoff gracefully; emit metric tenant_deflect_count. Also capture 1m of packet traces during canary.
Harper: Canary plan: roll to one hot-rack in eu-west at 22:30 UTC for 30m. Monitor: node_nic_queue_len_p95, nic_tx_drops, gpu_p99, tenant_deflect_count, client_429_rate.
Noah: Product/billing note: Dedicated customers expect isolation. This will be opt-in beta or compensated if we apply without opt-in. Loop in billing/legal before broad rollout.
ops-bot: Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/packet-spray-deflector. Canary ticket created: #PSP-1001.
Ivy: +10m into canary: deflections for T-alpha and T-omega, nic_queue_len down ~40%, GPU p99 improved from ~200ms -> ~35ms, client 5xx unchanged.
ops-bot: Canary completed at 1725000024 — status: success.
Harper: Next steps: open infra epic, add tenant_deflect_count and deflection_latency to dashboards, schedule billing/legal sync, and research SmartNIC/eBPF QoS for longer-term per-tenant isolation.
